key_insight: AutoPass uses evidence from the compiler and runtime feedback to let LLM agents systematically tune compiler optimizations for better performance.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical, training-free way to improve real program speed on different architectures without requiring task-specific fine-tuning.
method: Multi-agent LLM framework that queries LLVM internal optimization states and IR details.
Iteratively edits compiler options using measured runtime results to detect regressions and refine choices.
Combines compiler evidence with runtime feedback instead of treating the compiler as a black box.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on LLVM across server-grade x86-64 and embedded ARM64 systems, where it achieved geometric-mean speedups of 1.043x and 1.117x over LLVM -O3.
watch_item: Performance tuning depends on noisy runtime measurements and compiler-specific internals, so gains may vary by benchmark, hardware, and LLVM version.
paper_title: AutoPass: Evidence-Guided LLM Agents for Compiler Performance Tuning
